lines.trans: Three hours of work, ladies—behold the Official Thirtieth Anniversary Courtyard Seating Plan!
My goodness, Mazen, your blue fountain-pen lettering looks like a royal concert programme!
Table One under the tree for our Room Eight mapmaker, Suad, and number ten!
Every neighbour from Jasmine Street sits beside someone who shares their favourite tea or hobby!
Let me copy those twenty-eight seat numbers into the heavy paper ledger right now, Mazen.
Copy it? Why hide a work of art inside a dusty pencil notebook, Nour?
Fountain-pen ink does run rather quickly if even two drops of water touch it, Mazen.
There is not a single raincloud in Amman today, Suad—pure golden sunshine!
Yes, sunshine plus strong Friday wind whistling down Jasmine Street right outside the gate!
I shall carry this poster firmly in both hands straight to the wooden easel outside.
At least slide your reading glasses onto your nose before you cross the threshold!
Watch and learn—nothing could possibly happen between Room Nine and table one!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective.

examples.trans: At least the bread is ready in the oven.
We need less than ten minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أنوف.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your nose now.
The air feels cold on my nose in the morning.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmation ('yes! / exactly!').

examples.text: أيوا، هاد هو اللحن اللي كنت أدور عليه!
examples.trans: Yes, that's the exact melody I was looking for!

examples.text: أيوا بالزبط، حط الكراسي جنب القوس.
examples.trans: Yes, right there—put the chairs beside the arch.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمع.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Masculine noun with broken plural برامج (baraamij).

examples.text: برنامج الحفلة مطبوع على ورق أبيض.
examples.trans: The concert programme is printed on white paper.
What is our schedule for Saturday?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday praise word for anything beautifully crafted (تحفة فنية 'a work of art'). Plural: تحف.

examples.trans: Your lettering on paper is a work of art!
This old chair is a real treasure.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Form V reflexive of علّم ('to teach').

examples.text: نور بتتعلم شغل الاستقبال بسرعة كبيرة.
examples.trans: Nour is learning the front-desk work very quickly.
I learned to play the piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتفرج, بيتفرج).

examples.trans: Nobody gawks at the guests here!

examples.text: كنت ناوي تتفرج من الشارع المقابل؟
examples.trans: Were you planning to watch from across the street?

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'two' (إنتو التنين 'the two of you'); note homograph التنين ('Monday').

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'next to, beside'.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: From ح-م-ل ('to carry, hold'); names a music stand (حامل النوتة) or lamp/book holder.

examples.text: حطينا الورقة على حامل النوتة الخشب.
examples.trans: We set the sheet on the wooden music stand.

examples.text: حامل المفاتيح معلق ورا مكتب الاستقبال.
examples.trans: The key rack hangs behind the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحبار.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حفلات.

examples.trans: He designs concert halls.
We attended a lovely music concert.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبي, بيخبي).

examples.trans: Why did you save it away for me all these years?
She tucked the recipe away in the kitchen notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خرايط.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خطوط.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Classic Levantine word (from Turkish doğru) meaning 'straight ahead' in directions.

examples.trans: Turn left and walk straight to the bridge.
Walk straight to the end of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ذكريات.

examples.trans: This house is full of sweet memories.
Childhood memories are never forgotten.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Intensive profession pattern فعّال from رسم ('to draw'). Feminine: رسامة.

examples.text: ضيف غرفة تمانية رسام خرايط مشهور.
examples.trans: The Room Eight guest is a famous mapmaker.
The artist paints with watercolours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رسمية, plural: رسميين).

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for the guests only!
An official letter arrived in the noon post.

meanings.note: Paired with قلم in قلم رصاص ('pencil').

examples.trans: We write bookings in pencil.
The name is written in pencil underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرقام.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Hollow verb (يسيح / بيسيح). Used for ice melting, chocolate softening, or ink smearing in water.

examples.text: حبر القلم بيسيح إذا اجت عليه مي.
examples.trans: Pen ink runs if water gets on it.
The butter melted in the hot pan.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Respectful and warm Levantine title for a woman ('Madam / Mrs. / lady').

examples.text: يسلموا إيديكي يا ست سعاد عاللحن الحلو.
examples.trans: Bless your hands, Madam Suad, for the lovely melody.

examples.text: كل ست وشيخ بالحارة معزومين عالافتتاح.
examples.trans: Every lady and elder on the lane is invited to the opening.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.en: lady; madam; respectful title for a woman
meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of سيد ('sir/Mr.'); plural سيدات.

examples.text: أهلاً وسهلاً بالضيوف، تفضلوا يا سيدات.
examples.trans: Welcome guests, please come in, ladies.

examples.text: سألت سيدة بالشارع عن مكان الصيدلية.
examples.trans: I asked a lady in the street where the pharmacy is.

شاء.gloss: to will (إن شاء الله God willing)

meanings.en: to will (إن شاء الله God willing)
meanings.note: Used in everyday speech inside the fixed phrase إن شاء الله ('God willing / hopefully').

examples.trans: Everything alright, hopefully?
You will arrive safely, God willing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.en: to take part; participate; share something with
meanings.note: Form III verb (بشارك / شارك). Often followed by بـ ('participate in') or مع ('share with').

examples.trans: All the neighbours took part in hanging the lanterns.
Share your new idea for the project with us.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Singulative noun ('one tree') of collective شجر ('trees').

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أشغال.

examples.text: حبيت الشغل هون من أول يوم.
examples.trans: I loved the work here from day one.
Let us finish our work before noon.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite no -a ending.

examples.trans: The warm sun came out after the rain.
Read the card in the sunlight.

صار.gloss: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)

meanings.en: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Describes a pure musical note, clear sky (سما صافية), or clear broth.

examples.text: نغمة البيانو طلعت صافية متل المي.
examples.trans: The piano note rang out crystal clear.

examples.text: انشالله تضل السما صافية طول نهار التنين.
examples.trans: Hopefully the sky stays clear all day Monday.

meanings.en: to whistle (of a person or the wind)
meanings.note: Form II verb (بصفّر / صفّر) used for human whistling or wind whistling through wires and alleys.

examples.trans: The wind is whistling between the ropes.

examples.text: طارق صفّر لما شاف الفانوس طار لفوق.
examples.trans: Tariq whistled when he saw the lantern fly upward.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعبر, بيعبر).

examples.trans: Cross the overpass to downtown.
We crossed the street at the light.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عتبات.

examples.trans: We found the suitcase on the doorstep.
We swept the stone threshold in the morning.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Unit noun of collective غيم ('clouds'); plural غيوم. Frequently used in Levantine speech alongside سحابة.

examples.text: القمر عم بيطلع من ورا غيمة خفيفة.
examples.trans: The moon is peeking out from behind a light cloud.

examples.text: اليوم السما صافية وما فيها ولا غيمة.
examples.trans: Today the sky is clear with not a single cloud.

meanings.en: artistic; technical; relating to art or craft
meanings.note: Nisba adjective from فن ('art'): feminine فنية, plural فنيين. Means 'artistic' with work/taste and 'technical' with problems/details.

examples.text: كل فانوس فيه لمسة فنية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every lantern has a different artistic touch.

examples.text: صار معنا عطل فني بسيط بس حليناه.
examples.trans: We had a minor technical glitch, but we fixed it.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Spoken form of قراءة; كافيه قراية is a reading café.

examples.trans: Reading before sleep relaxes me.
My son loves reading.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقعد, بيقعد).

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قعدات.

examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard under the tree is cosy.

examples.text: قعدة الصبح مع القهوة ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: A morning sit-down with coffee is priceless.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural is قوايا (qawaaya): كرسيين قوايا ('two sturdy chairs').

examples.trans: The gate rang with one strong ring.
We brought two sturdy wooden chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كراسي.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمس, بيلمس).

examples.trans: Touch the radiator — it is warm on top.
Touch the brass pipe — it heated up!

meanings.note: Introduces polite requests (لو سمحت 'if you please') and hypothetical conditions ('if').

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'why?'.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Used for architectural/room floor plans, schedules, and blueprints.

examples.text: رسمنا المخطط الجديد للطاولات بملف الاستقبال.
examples.trans: We drew the new table floor plan in the front-desk folder.

examples.text: حسب المخطط في مكان مريح لست طاولات بالساحة.
examples.trans: According to the layout there is comfortable room for six tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستحيلة, plural: —).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
It is impossible for us to forget this week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أمطار.

examples.trans: Please come inside out of the cold rain.
The trees are green and lovely after the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Form II participle adjective (feminine مغبرة, plural مغبرين) from غبرة ('dust').

examples.text: الدرابزين كان مغبر قبل ما نمسحه.
examples.trans: The railing was dusty before we wiped it.
The old boxes in the storeroom are all dusty.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفضلة, plural: مفضلين).

examples.trans: This is my favourite cup for tea.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون هي الحلو المفضل عندهم.
examples.trans: Lemon cake is their favourite dessert.

meanings.en: royal; majestic; often used in أزرق ملكي ('royal blue')
meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ملك ('king'): feminine ملكية, plural ملكيين.

examples.text: صبغت السما بلون أزرق ملكي غامق.
examples.trans: I painted the sky in a deep royal blue colour.

examples.text: القصر الملكي مبين من فوق التلة.
examples.trans: The royal palace is visible from the top of the hill.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موسيقية, plural: موسيقيين).

examples.trans: Play the musical scale slowly.
She has a sensitive musical ear.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.en: to copy; trace a drawing; transcribe text
meanings.note: Form I verb (بنسخ / نسخ) used both for hand-copying drawings and copying text or files.

examples.text: نسخت الرسمة القديمة على ورقة نظيفة.
examples.trans: I copied the old drawing onto a clean sheet.

examples.text: ممكن تنسخ لي الوصفة على دفتري؟
examples.trans: Could you copy the recipe into my notebook for me?

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نقط.

examples.trans: Not a single drop of juice got on the table!

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من الشوربة السخنة.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the hot soup.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural هوايات) from هوى ('to be fond of / love').

examples.text: الرسم بالألوان المائية أحلى هواية عندي.
examples.trans: Watercolour painting is my favourite hobby.
What are your favourite hobbies in your free time?

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: With two pronunciations in context: walla ('or' in choice questions: عالشارع ولا عالساحة؟) and wala ('not even / nor': ولا خدش 'not a single scratch', ولا يهمك 'do not worry at all').

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
